review_type: Second intensive, source-led review of three public-registry-labelled samples
source_policy: No malware feed, advisory, scanner reputation or classifier score is used as proof. All three original hashes verified; no reconstruction or external fetch required.
commands: atomscan <sample> and cleave facts <sample> for all originals
env GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build -o <scratch>/gentlemen-review.exe <sample>
make validate is the required final gate; its actual result is reported in the final response

device_relay_review.execution: The IIFE POSTs /api/device/start with a fixed 64-hex anti-bot header; destructures user_code/session_id; displays and copies the code; opens the genuine Microsoft device-login page on click; every five seconds GETs same-origin status for the encoded session identifier; stops polling and redirects to /document on completed.
device_relay_review.intent_balance: MALICIOUS: shared-document verification is the presented pretext for authorizing a device session brokered by this page. The anti-bot gated handoff and completion redirect support a phishing relay. A first-party document portal could legitimately broker authentication, but no application/client disclosure, ownership context, or authorizing backend accompanies this artifact. This is a likelihood judgement, not proof of completed token theft.
device_relay_review.limits: The backend and OAuth client/scopes are absent. The page neither receives an OAuth access token nor sends it to an external collector. The header is constant; no time-hash, obfuscation, decryption, persistence or execution stage exists in these bytes.
device_relay_review.coverage_goal: Two hostile findings retained: document-pretext device-session relay and copying the relayed authorization code. The entire inline script and prior document/device-login controls were inspected and rescanned. A third distinct hostile behavior is unsupported without the backend; network, clipboard, timers and navigation are already covered as notable capabilities. No quota-driven duplicate is added.
device_relay_review.classifier_disagreement: Final slow local model remains BENIGN (calibrated level -1) despite two accurate hostile rules. Raw probability 0.9956313 is not a calibrated conviction. Balanced tiny output also said benign while reporting bloom=known-bad; neither the bloom label nor its uncorroborated registry conviction establishes intent.

gentlemen_review.execution: The password gate precedes all activity. On acceptance main raises priority, calls native process information APIs, launches Defender-disable/exclusion commands, deletes Prefetch/Defender/RDP logs and PowerShell history, clears three Windows event logs, kills named VM/database/backup processes, disables/stops backup and security services, creates an ONSTART SYSTEM task with ONLOGON fallback, writes HKLM/HKCU Run keys, deletes VSS/WMIC shadows, disables firewall profiles, and queries volume roots.
gentlemen_review.payload_limits: prepareAndEncryptFile takes ownership, grants Everyone full control and clears read-only before opening a target. It only generates random key/nonce bytes, Base64-encodes them, appends a Gentlemen-labelled footer and optionally renames the file. It never transforms file contents cryptographically. main feeds volume directory roots, not a recursive file walk, so opening them as regular writable files is likely to fail before footer writing. Static capability and attempted sabotage are distinct from runtime success.
gentlemen_review.unused_claims: path, delay, SYSTEM and spread options, ECDH public key, ransom-note constant, excluded-directory/file lists are not used to implement their advertised behavior. No ECDH/key wrapping, ransom-note write, recursive encryption, wallpaper, lateral propagation or real share enumeration/targeting exists. The --shares branch only runs net use for drive letters and discards its results.
gentlemen_review.optional_effects: --wipe queries C: free bytes, writes a fresh zero-initialized buffer repeatedly to a temporary file until that size is attempted, then deletes it. Without --keep, it writes a temporary batch script, launches cmd, delays with loopback ping, deletes the original executable and then %~f0. Write/permission/child-process errors are mostly ignored.
gentlemen_review.encoding_and_native_call: The embedded Base64 public key decodes to 32 bytes but is unused. The footer is plaintext Base64 of 32 random bytes plus a 12-byte nonce; it is not encrypted key material. NtSetInformationProcess is called with numeric class 0x21; the helper name alone does not establish exception-port manipulation or debugger evasion, so no such objective is added.
gentlemen_review.intent_balance: MALICIOUS even as an incomplete locker: active defense blinding, backup destruction, forensic cleanup, durable reactivation and optional free-space overwrite outweigh the absence of a working encryption payload. Cross-compilation for Windows succeeds. No specimen binary or external command was executed.

fort_review.execution: CLI reads explicit targets and submits threaded tasks. Each task first generates matching random username/password and POSTs an administrator-creation body (prof_admin, trusthostv4 0.0.0.0/0) to an admin API path traversing into fwbcgi. CGIINFO is Base64 JSON forging admin/prof_admin/root context. A 200 response triggers a GET check with Basic auth for the new credentials.
fort_review.fallback: If exploit verification fails, the tool iterates a 4x4 default username/password product against /logincheck. It honors a 60-second lockout response and recognizes a session-cookie success. All requests explicitly use verify=False.
fort_review.credential_recovery: With --parse-configs and an accepted user, it GETs the global configuration backup, selects password/passwd ENC fields, Base64-decodes each, constructs an IV from the first four bytes plus twelve zeros, and calls AES-CBC decrypt with the embedded 16-byte default configuration key. Returned plaintext is stripped of zero padding.
fort_review.limits: The creation/bypass function name is not proof of a particular CVE or product version. The mixed FortiWeb handler and FortiOS API paths may fail on real targets. Cookies from the supplied Session, rather than the returned Basic-auth tuple, govern the later backup request. There is no payload download, external exfiltration collector, covert persistence hook, or automatic registry-install execution. Main discards task return values; recovered secrets are not printed/saved. CIS_EXCLUDED, --no-exclude and --combine are unused: no geofencing or operator-wordlist loading occurs.
fort_review.intent_balance: MALICIOUS from the balance of behavior: it defaults to intrusive auth bypass with a durable unrestricted administrator, then password guessing and optional plaintext secret recovery, without account cleanup. The scanner banner and operator target list make authorized penetration testing plausible, but no engagement/authorization context or benign deployment accompanies this copy. Generic password recovery is separately kept suspicious, since administrators can legitimately recover their own backups.
fort_review.offline_checks: Mocked request/crypto boundaries verified the exact forged CGIINFO JSON, creation fields, Basic-auth check, lockout sleep, password submission and decrypt arguments. These traces are not evidence of target exploitation success or actual AES output.

rule_corrections.change: Relocate all three option observations out of ransomware/encrypt; rename at notable and preserve matchers, proximity, scope and consumers.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Password, spread/GPO, shares, fast or path options alone prove neither encryption nor spreading. Neutral CLI control matches the old grammar and has no hostile behavior. Original Go sabotage/family detections remain.

rule_corrections.change: Move recovery/ACL/log-clear composite to impact/degrade/system/recovery unchanged.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: No extortion or encryption is required by this matcher, so ransom placement was unsupported.

rule_corrections.change: Move both Windows firewall-disable command atoms to os/security/firewall and update the existing impairment composite.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Command text records configuration mechanics; neither named command alone proves attacker intent. Exact command observations and higher-level impairment detection remain.

rule_corrections.change: Relocate FortiWeb forged-session traversal rule from lateral movement to service exploitation; remove account-creation wording; preserve every required leg and scope.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: The old matcher had no creation body or established cross-host lateral deployment. It does identify forged administrator-session traversal.

rule_corrections.change: Narrow unrestricted-admin persistence to an exploit context and an exact trusthostv4=0.0.0.0/0 field, with HTTP submission and password evidence.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Any CIDR /24 or wider could previously be called unrestricted; ordinary API provisioning also matched. Both restricted and unrestricted legitimate provisioning controls now avoid the hostile finding.

rule_corrections.change: Retain default-key ENC recovery as suspicious and require an actual decrypt-method call.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: Key/Base64/API/password strings alone did not establish decryption. Authorized offline configuration-password recovery is a concrete benign use; no hostile claim is justified by this operation alone.

rule_corrections.change: Relocate shell:true object-property matcher to data/property/assign, preserving matcher/scope/notable level and all explicit consumers/fixtures.
rule_corrections.unsupported_claim: An arbitrary object field is not necessarily a process argument. This previously reviewed observation was re-audited in the full 100-rule option leaf; moving it corrects its subject rather than hiding or deleting a rule to gain capacity.

rule_corrections.change: Add Go startup/logon actions, malicious reactivation with whole-drive Defender blinding, service-disable/recovery sabotage, self-removal, Prefetch/history cleanup, disk-free sizing, zero-initialized writes; add Python credential-pair guessing and per-request TLS disable.
rule_corrections.coverage: Detections require source content and general behavior/field/API grammar, not sample hashes, chosen task names, a chosen C2 domain or collector filenames.

shared_consumer_audit.option_leaf: Reviewed the complete option catalog before adding the generalizable spread/GPO atom. Password-option co-occurrence profiles fit argument/credential. The shell:true atom was a misplaced property observation; no directory budget was raised and no new taxonomy partition was invented.
shared_consumer_audit.shell_property_parent: The property/assign ancestor is used by long-tail-build-config-payload. This parent now correctly sees shell:true as a property assignment; its build-config, long-tail and concealment requirements remain mandatory. The ordinary shell-option and actual spawn fixtures remain non-hostile.
shared_consumer_audit.recovery_parent: The only found objectives/impact ancestor consumer is a CrystalX family exclusion; the moved composite was already in that ancestor, so membership is preserved.
shared_consumer_audit.other_consumers: The ESXi hidden-daemon rule retains the same CLI option profile through its renamed neutral reference. Firewall composites retain both exact command atoms. No exact external consumer of the moved FortiWeb or recovery-ACL-log ID was found.

material_detection_losses: No supported behavior is removed from these three originals. One unsupported Go hostile spread/encryption-CLI assertion and one suspicious ransomware-CLI assertion become neutral CLI observations. Fort default-key recovery moves hostile->suspicious, with mere references excluded. Relocations retain their actual observations; new independent behavior detections are not score substitutes.

verification.decoded_or_extracted_stages: No concealed executable stage or archive member exists in these three plain source artifacts. Base64 transformations and the embedded batch template were traced explicitly.
verification.model_warning: Installed model feature schema v18 is older than expected v21. The remaining HTML calibrated miss is reported without altering accurate rules to manipulate its score.
